findings.summary: Delete, archive, park, unpark or a reused id can strip a finding of its lane gate; several writers can overwrite a blocked lane's status; legacy history, the cap after unblock and restore-main handle gate rows inconsistently; and the batch finalizer changes lanes the batch did not mean to change.

findings.title: Introspect does not look across rounds and PRs for repeated waste
findings.summary: Introspect does not scan across rounds for repeated waste, and no workflow-level Introspect runs after a merge to gate the next Collect.
findings.impact: Patterns that repeat across lanes and rounds (review loops, interrupted runs, retries, token-heavy steps, hand work outside bcl) are never reviewed as a whole, so they recur in the next PR.
findings.recommendation: Add a cross-round scan to the Introspect draft that requires a workflow change when a kind repeats, replacing free-form repeat notes; add a post-merge Introspect over the whole PR's measured job data that names repeating patterns, records cuts in the order delete, simplify, optimize, automate, and gates the next Collect. Seed the draft from the observability issues of the round's verify window and require a finding key or evidence path on every item, flagging or dropping items without one. Report tokens used per round and per group, step and job from observability task usage, compared with the previous round; name any missing token source (Codex or Grok Bot subagents) and include adding it. Judge whether the observability evidence was correct and useful (missing kinds, noise, stale data, wrong attribution) and file needed observability fixes as DO issues through add or into.
findings.done_when: Introspect flags repeats across rounds with a required change, and the next PR's Collect is refused until the post-merge Introspect is recorded; tests cover both. Each Introspect item cites a finding key or evidence path or is flagged; the Introspect shows tokens per round and per group, step and job with the previous round's figures, or names the missing source; it records an evidence-quality verdict and files or appends DO issues for gaps; tests cover each.

findings.title: Snapshot commits made by the change list show as unpushed-commit failures
findings.summary: The collector reports an unpushed-commits failure for the pull request checkout whenever the change list has just committed its own tracker snapshot, which is expected and pushed minutes later.
findings.impact: The only new finding between the before and after snapshots of a verify was this noise, so verify evidence is diluted.
findings.recommendation: Treat unpushed commits that only touch the change list's own tracker snapshot files as expected, or report unpushed commits as a state rather than a failure.
findings.done_when: A verify that commits a tracker snapshot adds no failure finding; a test covers it.

findings.title: No per-round view: earlier rounds' findings mix with the current one
findings.summary: A snapshot lists every finding for a project with no round or window filter, so this round's view of the plugin repository mixed 3 active findings with 20 stale ones from 14 and 20 November, and no finding carries a project field for the change list.
findings.impact: An agent acting on the snapshot reads old failures as current and spends context on them.
findings.recommendation: Stamp each event with pull request, round, stage, plugin, group, job and run at capture, from the change list's event log; extend the existing issues query with those filters plus change class and a time window, returning a capped one-line summary first and rows, one finding, and evidence paths only on request; apply noise rules. No new tool, no dashboard.
findings.done_when: The ten acceptance checks in the spec pass: round queries return only that round's stamped rows with unstamped counts and gaps, change classes are correct, tier caps and noise rules hold, and the cursor is bound to the filters. The app UI shows the same view, filters, drill-down and a per-round timeline of steps and jobs with tokens and outcomes, through the same query as the agent, with readable fonts and zoom and text-size controls.

findings.title: A change list only release runs every plugin's slowest suites
findings.summary: The full suite for a lane that changes only the change list plugin also runs the agent computer use Swift service tests and other plugins' slow suites, which dominate its two and a half minutes.
findings.impact: Each release waits on unrelated suites; three releases today spent about seven and a half minutes in full suites.
findings.recommendation: Keep the full suite for merge and CI parity, but let a lane's release suite run the changed plugins' tests plus the repository contract checks, and record which suites were skipped.
findings.done_when: A change list only release runs only its plugin's tests and the contract checks, shows the skipped suites, and the merge still runs everything.
